seeds.title: Projects page status model is setup-centric
seeds.summary: Current project card health/status representation emphasizes repo and config integrity but does not capture operational attention semantics.
evidence: The Projects page currently covers name/path, language badges, last opened, orchestrator status, and health indicator.
Health indicators are mostly repo/config existence checks (green/amber/red).
The model is described as useful but insufficient for blocked ownership, attention reason, pressure, and activity posture.

seeds.title: Split project card state into health, activity, attention
seeds.summary: Recommended decomposition separates integrity signals from runtime posture and actionability to avoid overloaded status dots.
evidence: Recommendation explicitly separates project health, project activity, and project attention.
Activity model candidate: idle, running, paused, queued, background_active.
Attention model candidate: none, attention_required, blocked, degraded.

seeds.title: Add blocked/attention owner and primary reason
seeds.summary: Project cards should show dominant owner and one primary reason instead of listing every issue.
evidence: Blocked-owner seam is called out as underdefined and should answer who/what the project is waiting on.
Owner kinds are enumerated (Runtime, Package Overseer, Seam Overseer, Corroboration, Graph Patch, Recovery, User, External Resource).
Recommendation is one primary attention/blocked reason with optional count badge for additional issues.

seeds.title: Surface compact pressure summary on project card
seeds.summary: Cards should expose concise provider/account pressure indicators and confidence without full usage detail.
evidence: Pressure summary direction asks for compact signals rather than detailed usage breakdown.
Examples include provider pressure, account switch, and quota signal confidence.
Recommendation keeps details behind deep links to Usage/Authentication/Orchestrator.

seeds.title: Differentiate active, recent, and historical posture
seeds.summary: Historical-only run presence should not be treated as degradation or blocked state unless explicit archival semantics exist.
evidence: Docs recommend avoiding a semantic class of historical project unless archiving is introduced.
Suggested distinction is active workspace/project, recently active, and archived/unregistered.
A project with only historical runs is explicitly stated as not inherently problematic.

seeds.title: Represent background activity independently
seeds.summary: Background work should be visible as its own state and should not be conflated with blocked attention.
evidence: Background activity is called out as important at project-card level.
Rule recommends surfacing background work independently from blocked attention.
Example allows background_active and attention_required simultaneously without global blocked.

seeds.title: Project page should consume canonical rollup projection
seeds.summary: Projects view should summarize canonical project-level projections from orchestrator-related sources, not invent local status semantics.
evidence: Recommendation is to summarize from canonical project-level projections.
Proposed rollup includes active run state, dominant concern owner, highest-severity attention, pressure summary, and health integrity.
Candidate fix defines a compact project-summary projection with singular dominant reason.

seeds.title: Define shared notification escalation ladder
seeds.summary: Cross-surface notification handling should use a single severity progression ending in selective system notifications.
evidence: Current behavior is described as many case-by-case local attention mechanisms.
Recommended shared progression: info, warning, attention_required, blocked, system_notification.
System notifications are reserved for high-value sparse events while history captures everything.

seeds.title: Map escalation levels to UI surfaces
seeds.summary: Severity should determine where and how signals appear, from history-first logging to selective chat and OS-level interruption.
evidence: History should receive everything chronologically.
Progress/Dashboard should show active warning, attention, and blocked states with compressed badge markers.
Chat/thread should be reserved for items requiring user decision/input; system notifications for sparse high-value events.
